data.narrative:
Toka, a Series B defense and security company founded by Yaron Rosen, Kfir Waldman, and Alon Kantor, has raised $38M to date. Valuation analysis draws on two methodologies applied to a peer universe of 10 comparable companies across the Defense & Security sector: 8 private firms and 2 public equities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $38M total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B progression to subsequent stages, implies a valuation of $72M. Peer-median analysis relies on six same-sector, same-stage private comparables—Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Defense Unicorns ($1.0B), Heven AeroTech ($1.0B), and one additional peer—which establish a median valuation of $1.1B against a range of $300M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $61M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $599M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Toka's market positioning relative to the peer set. The peer cohort shows substantial heterogeneity; the $72M stage-progression result sits materially below the median, suggesting either that Toka is earlier in development trajectory relative to comps or that the peer set skews toward later-stage or better-capitalized entrants. Key unknowns include Toka's revenue run rate, customer concentration, and technology differentiation within the crowded defense-tech landscape.
